storyboard.title: One query's guardrails
storyboard.authoredBy: Hand-written (Opus, arc build) as the first story-arc video: a walkthrough arc over litefleet's pinned dataset and code. Narration spoken forms follow the POCs' rules: numbers, symbols and file names are spelled for TTS in speech, kept exact in captions.

lines.caption: Litefleet: a small multitenant SQLite platform, one owning node per database.
lines.speech: Litefleet is a small multitenant SQLite platform, with one owning node per database.

lines.caption: It was built lesson by lesson, following the book Release It!
lines.speech: It was built lesson by lesson, following the book Release It.

lines.caption: This video follows one query, pinned at release-it/v1-hardened.
lines.speech: This video follows one query through it, pinned at the release-it v1 hardened tag.

scenes.caption: Tenants send SQL to Litefleet with an API key. Let's open it up.
Gateways route each query to the node agent that owns its database.
Inside the node, every statement passes the admission engine first.

lines.caption: The admission and SQL engine decides if a statement may run, and for how long.
It checks the epoch, takes a database lane, then tenant and node slots.
And it bounds every statement with a 2 second deadline.
lines.speech: And it bounds every statement with a two second deadline.

lines.caption: Engine.Query in exec.go, at the pinned commit: every read enters here.
lines.speech: Here is Engine dot Query, in exec dot go. Every read enters here.

lines.caption: Guard one, the deadline: the context gets 2 seconds, then it is cancelled.
lines.speech: Guard one is the deadline. The context gets two seconds, then it is cancelled.

lines.caption: Guard two, the bulkheads: acquire takes a lane and slots, or refuses.
lines.speech: Guard two is the bulkheads. Acquire takes a lane and slots, or refuses.

scenes.caption: Why 2 s? The gateway allows 2.9 s, so a timeout still gets its 504 back.
scenes.speech: Why two seconds? The gateway allows two point nine, so a timed-out statement still gets its five-oh-four back in time.

lines.caption: The bulkheads, per database: 2 readers, 1 writer and 8 waiting.
lines.speech: The bulkheads, per database: two readers, one writer, and eight waiting.

lines.caption: Then 4 statements per tenant across the node, and 16 for the whole node.
lines.speech: Then four statements per tenant across the node, and sixteen for the whole node.

lines.caption: So one tenant can hold at most a quarter of the node.

scenes.caption: Guard three caps the answer: 1000 rows or 1 MiB of JSON, whichever first.
scenes.speech: Guard three caps the answer: one thousand rows, or one mebibyte of JSON, whichever comes first.

lines.caption: In the scan loop, either cap stops the stream, and the answer says truncated.
Bounded time, bounded concurrency, bounded answers: one query's guardrails.
Git blame credits every line shown to nickstrad, across seven commits.
lines.speech: Git blame credits every line shown to Nick Strad, across seven commits.

captions.text: Litefleet: a small multitenant SQLite platform, one owning node per database.
It was built lesson by lesson, following the book Release It!
This video follows one query, pinned at release-it/v1-hardened.
Tenants send SQL to Litefleet with an API key. Let's open it up.
Gateways route each query to the node agent that owns its database.
Inside the node, every statement passes the admission engine first.
The admission and SQL engine decides if a statement may run, and for how long.
It checks the epoch, takes a database lane, then tenant and node slots.
And it bounds every statement with a 2 second deadline.
Engine.Query in exec.go, at the pinned commit: every read enters here.
Guard one, the deadline: the context gets 2 seconds, then it is cancelled.
Guard two, the bulkheads: acquire takes a lane and slots, or refuses.
Why 2 s? The gateway allows 2.9 s, so a timeout still gets its 504 back.
The bulkheads, per database: 2 readers, 1 writer and 8 waiting.
Then 4 statements per tenant across the node, and 16 for the whole node.
So one tenant can hold at most a quarter of the node.
Guard three caps the answer: 1000 rows or 1 MiB of JSON, whichever first.
In the scan loop, either cap stops the stream, and the answer says truncated.
Bounded time, bounded concurrency, bounded answers: one query's guardrails.
Git blame credits every line shown to nickstrad, across seven commits.
Thanks for watching.
